newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: US gives $70 million to UN refugee agency, Red Cross.
newsitem.headline: US gives $70 million to UN refugee agency, Red Cross.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday it had contributed more than $70 million to four international humanitarian agencies helping refugees and displaced civilians in former Yugoslavia, Rwanda, Burundi and elsewhere.
The bulk of the voluntary contributions, $48.6 million, will go to the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), including $30 million to aid displaced Rwandans and Burundians.

The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) will receive $6.33 million, roughly half of which is targeted to help civilians in Chechnya; the Geneva-based International Organisation for Migration, which arranges movement of refugees and migrants to new homes, will receive $3.7 million; and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies will recieve $1 million for its work in former Yugoslavia.

"The voluntary contributions will cover essential assistance programmes for refugees, displaced people and other vulnerable people in the former Yugoslavia, Rwanda, Burundi, Burma and elsewhere," the U.S. diplomatic mission said in a statement.

Daniel Spiegel, U.S. ambassador to the United Nations in Geneva, was quoted as saying: "These programmes provide essential aid to hundreds of thousands of people in the former Yugoslavia, Rwanda, Burundi and other troubled regions of the world. They shelter the homeless, feed the hungry and provide hope to those most in in need."
In addition, the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) has donated $10 million to UNHCR's programmes for Cyprus.
"The United States was the largest single contributor to UNHCR, ICRC and IOM in 1995 and is the largest contributor to date in 1996," the U.S. statement said.
